findings.detail: PyMem_Malloc() size argument multiplies a Python-controlled operand (argcount) with no visible overflow guard (no PY_SSIZE_T_MAX/size division check, < 0 sign check, or __builtin_mul_overflow before the call). The product can wrap, under-allocating the buffer (bug class R5; cf. gh-3493, gh-1779). Use PyMem_New/PyMem_Calloc (they overflow-check) or add an explicit `n > PY_SSIZE_T_MAX / size` guard.

'op' is allocated via PyObject_GC_New() and freed with Py_DECREF() on an error path before any PyObject_GC_Track(op) — if tp_dealloc runs the untrack macro (_PyObject_GC_UNTRACK) on the never-tracked object the GC invariant is violated (bug class O6; cf. gh-152107 OOM-0006/0017). Ensure the error path does not reach an unconditional untrack, or track before the fallible step.
